ai.definition: Synthetic Carbon Capture Organisms are engineered microorganisms designed to hyper-efficiently fix carbon dioxide from the atmosphere, converting it directly into stable biopolymers. These organisms are optimized for the Calvin cycle and incorporate new synthetic metabolic pathways.
ai.howItWorks: These organisms are genetically modified to enhance their ability to capture CO2 through the optimization of the Calvin cycle, a process used by plants to convert carbon dioxide into organic compounds. Additionally, they have been engineered with synthetic metabolic pathways that allow them to directly convert captured CO2 into biopolymers, which can be harvested and utilized in various applications.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing atmospheric CO2 levels and promoting sustainable materials production through biological means.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves genetic engineering of microorganisms, typically bacteria or algae, to include synthetic metabolic pathways that enhance their carbon fixation capabilities. These organisms are then cultured under controlled conditions for mass production.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes gene synthesis and assembly, followed by the integration of these genes into host microorganisms using techniques such as CRISPR-Cas9. The resulting organisms are then tested in laboratory settings before scaling up to industrial-scale operations.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the initial genetic engineering and synthesis costs, along with ongoing maintenance and scale-up expenses. Environmental factors like temperature and pH also impact cost efficiency.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to transition from lab research to early commercial stages within the next few years as more successful trials are conducted and regulatory frameworks are established.
ai.regulation: Current regulation is limited, but as the technology advances, environmental and biosafety regulations will likely be developed. This includes assessing the potential impact on ecosystems and ensuring the safe disposal of biopolymers.
ai.risks: Risks include unintended ecological impacts from releasing genetically modified organisms into the environment, potential issues with biopolymer degradation, and challenges in scaling production while maintaining efficiency.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain but could be significant if successful. The ability to create valuable biopolymers from CO2 reduction efforts has the potential for substantial market value.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will focus on improving the efficiency of carbon capture, expanding the range of biopolymers produced, and ensuring robust regulatory compliance.

glossary.def: A metabolic pathway used by plants to convert carbon dioxide into organic compounds.
Polymers derived from biological sources, often used in various industrial applications.

subsystems.name: Engineered microbe
subsystems.role: the living catalyst that fixes CO2 and converts it into biopolymer.

subsystems.name: CO2 supply and delivery
subsystems.role: provides concentrated CO2 to the bioreactor.

subsystems.name: Bioreactor
subsystems.role: controlled environment for growth and production.
parts: temperature, pH and dissolved gas sensors

subsystems.name: Metabolic pathway
subsystems.role: converts CO2 into precursor molecules for polymer synthesis.

subsystems.name: Polymer synthesis
subsystems.role: assembles precursors into a stable biopolymer.

subsystems.name: Downstream processing
subsystems.role: harvests cells and extracts the biopolymer.

subsystems.name: Containment and safety
subsystems.role: prevents escape and survival of engineered organisms.

buildSteps.title: Select chassis organism
buildSteps.detail: Choose a fast-growing, genetically tractable microbe that can use CO2 as its main carbon source, such as a cyanobacterium or an acetogen.

buildSteps.title: Engineer carbon fixation
buildSteps.detail: Introduce or enhance genes for efficient CO2 fixation, possibly using a synthetic or optimised natural cycle to boost carbon uptake.

buildSteps.title: Optimise metabolic flux
buildSteps.detail: Tune gene expression and enzyme activity so most fixed carbon flows toward the desired polymer precursor rather than being wasted.

buildSteps.title: Add polymer pathway
buildSteps.detail: Insert genes for biopolymer synthesis, such as polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA) enzymes, so the cell accumulates the polymer as granules.

buildSteps.title: Design bioreactor
buildSteps.detail: Build a closed system that delivers CO2 efficiently to the culture, controls light or chemical energy, and maintains optimal growth conditions.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Move from lab flasks to pilot-scale bioreactors, testing gas transfer rates, productivity and contamination control at larger volumes.

buildSteps.title: Harvest and extract
buildSteps.detail: Develop cost-effective methods to separate cells from broth, break them open, and purify the biopolymer without degrading it.

buildSteps.title: Test stability and safety
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the polymer is stable for its intended use and that the engineered organism cannot survive or spread outside the bioreactor.

buildSteps.title: Life-cycle analysis
buildSteps.detail: Verify net carbon removal and economic viability, including energy use, CO2 source, and end-of-life for the polymer.

prerequisites.why: gene synthesis, CRISPR editing and promoter libraries are needed to rewire microbial metabolism.
commercial plants already use microbes to ferment industrial waste gases into ethanol, proving the core process.
many microbes make PHA naturally, but engineering them to do so efficiently from CO2 at scale is not yet demonstrated.
capturing CO2 from flue gas or air is technically feasible but still costly and energy-intensive.
gas fermenters exist, but optimising them for CO2 and polymer accumulation remains a scale-up challenge.
kill switches and physical barriers have been demonstrated in labs, but long-term reliability at industrial scale is unproven.

pathway.milestone: engineered microbes produce measurable biopolymer from CO2 in small-scale cultures.
pathway.unlocks: validation of the core metabolic design.

pathway.milestone: integrated pilot plant runs continuously on a real CO2 source, such as cement or steel off-gas.
pathway.unlocks: data on productivity, stability and operating costs.

pathway.milestone: first plants converting captured CO2 to biopolymers at kiloton-per-year scale.
pathway.unlocks: a market-ready product and a credible carbon-removal route.

pathway.milestone: widespread adoption linked to carbon capture networks and material supply chains.
pathway.unlocks: meaningful atmospheric carbon drawdown alongside fossil-free materials.
